name: Brooklyn Bridge
short_description: Iconic global landmark, extensive Wikipedia coverage, National Historic Landmark, millions of annual pedestrians. Top-tier gravity. Note: coordinate is mid-span; Manhattan-tower-specific trigger may warrant a sub-POI later.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Iconic global landmark, extensive Wikipedia coverage, National Historic Landmark, millions of annual pedestrians. Top-tier gravity. Note: coordinate is mid-span; Manhattan-tower-specific trigger may warrant a sub-POI later.

beats.script_body: Walking the span of the Brooklyn Bridge lets you see this marvel of engineering up close. When it was built in 1883, it was the longest suspension bridge in the world. Look up and down the East River, and you also get a close-up of the bridge's massive Gothic brownstone towers.

physical_cues.cue: Massive Gothic brownstone towers of the bridge
Views up and down the East River from the walkway

key_claims: longest suspension bridge in the world when built
beats.source_passage:
Walking the Brooklyn Bridge: The bridge, too, offers glorious views of the
city. But that’s not the only reason you stroll here: Walking the span
allows you to see this marvel of engineering up close. (It was the
longest suspension bridge in the world when it was built in 1883.). See
page 171.

source_attribution.author: Pauline Frommer
source_attribution.chapter: Chapter 1: The Best of the Big Apple

name: Chrysler Building
short_description: Iconic Art Deco skyscraper, named by Frommer's as best NYC skyscraper and New Yorkers' favorite. High-gravity landmark.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Iconic Art Deco skyscraper, named by Frommer's as best NYC skyscraper and New Yorkers' favorite. High-gravity landmark.

beats.script_body: When asked, most New Yorkers would name the Art Deco spire of the Chrysler Building as their favorite Manhattan skyscraper. Its sleek hood-ornament spire is as jaunty as ever, a heartening sight to behold. The Chrysler has no observation deck, but this Art Deco masterpiece can be viewed from outside, or from nearby observation decks such as the Empire State Building's.

name: Grand Central Terminal
short_description: Major Beaux Arts transit landmark, Frommer's 'best historic building'. High gravity.

beats.script_body: Grand Central Station is a Beaux Arts gem. This iconic railroad station, built in 1913, was restored in the 1990s to its original brilliance. More than just a thriving transit hub, it rewards a closer look — you can take a walking tour with the help of a smartphone once you're inside the building.

name: Domino Park
short_description: Newer waterfront park on the former sugar refinery site; Frommer's parks pick. Moderate gravity.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Newer waterfront park on the former sugar refinery site; Frommer's parks pick. Moderate gravity.

beats.script_body: Domino Park is set on the grounds of what was once the largest sugar refinery on the planet. The park artfully incorporates many of the industrial artifacts that were left behind, and offers sweeping views of Manhattan along with a great collection of eateries and drinkeries for those who want to linger.

name: Brooklyn Heights
short_description: First NYC historic district; strolling neighborhood with famous promenade. Moderate gravity.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: First NYC historic district; strolling neighborhood with famous promenade. Moderate gravity.

beats.script_body: Brooklyn Heights was the very first designated historic district in New York City, and you'll understand why when you stroll through its blocks of pristine 19th-century row houses, brownstones, and mansions. There is no better view of Manhattan and New York Harbor than from the Heights' famous promenade.

name: Roosevelt Island Tram
short_description: Aerial tram with skyline views; 'see NYC like a local' pick. Moderate gravity.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Aerial tram with skyline views; 'see NYC like a local' pick. Moderate gravity.

beats.script_body: The Roosevelt Island Tram may be just a 4-minute ride, but the views are spectacular, and it carries you to an island very few outsiders ever visit. It runs beside the 59th Street Bridge — also known as the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge — and it has become even more worth the effort since the FDR Four Freedoms Park opened at Roosevelt Island's tip.

Freedoms Park opened at Roosevelt Island’s tip. See p. 214.
